script:
export const meta = {
  name: 'punctuation-sweep-design-file',
  description: 'Sweep banned punctuation from seven chunks of ring-buffer-design.md',
  phases: [{ title: 'Sweep' }],
}
const RULES = `You are editing one chunk of a markdown design document in place, with the Edit tool. The job is punctuation only. Do not change meaning, do not add or drop facts, do not touch headings' words, do not reflow text you do not otherwise change, and do not touch anything inside fenced code blocks (\`\`\`) or inline code spans (\`...\`).

Remove every one of these from the prose: the semicolon ";", the em dash "—", the en dash "–", the ellipsis "…", the arrow "→". Rules:

1. "…" becomes "..." and "→" becomes "->" (in prose only).
2. A bullet with a bold lead and an em dash, "- **Label** — text", becomes "- Label: text": drop the bold, replace " —" with ":". The same when the lead is not bold but the dash separates a term from its definition ("\`foo\` — what it is" becomes "\`foo\`: what it is"). If the label already ends in a colon or other punctuation, do not double it.
3. An em dash used as a prose aside becomes a comma, parentheses, or two sentences, whichever reads naturally. A pair of em dashes around an aside becomes a pair of commas or parentheses.
4. A semicolon joining two claims becomes a period, the second half capitalized as its own sentence. A semicolon where the second half continues the first becomes a comma with a conjunction ("and", "so", "but"). A semicolon at the END of a list item (a list written "- a;\\n- b;\\n- c.") is simply deleted, or becomes a period when the item is a full sentence. Several items joined by semicolons inside one sentence become sub-bullets, or commas when the items are short and hold no commas.
5. Keep lines at or under 100 columns. If a changed line grows past 100, re-wrap only that paragraph or bullet, continuation lines indented to match the existing ones.
6. Text that is a verbatim quotation of tool output or a commit title keeps its characters. When unsure, convert.

When done, verify with: awk '/^\`\`\`/{c=!c;next} !c' FILE | sed 's/\`[^\`]*\`//g' | grep -n '[;—–…→]'   and fix anything it prints that is not a verbatim quotation. Note that an inline code span broken across two lines can show as a false hit, leave those. Report only: the count of lines you changed, and any place you were unsure about (line and what you chose).`
const chunks = [1,2,3,4,5,6,7]
const results = await parallel(chunks.map(i => () =>
  agent(`${RULES}\n\nYour file is /home/wink/data/prgs/rust/zc-ring-x1/tmp/rbd/c${i}.md . Edit only that file.`, { label: `sweep:c${i}`, phase: 'Sweep', model: 'sonnet' })
))
return { results }

results:
Clean. No forbidden punctuation remains and no line exceeds 100 columns.

I changed roughly 90 lines across the file (Overview, Blue-sky goal, ISR gotcha bullets, Terminology, Requirements, Constraints, Execution contexts, Memory layout bullets, Index scheme, and the Ordering paragraph) in `/home/wink/data/prgs/rust/zc-ring-x1/tmp/rbd/c1.md`.

Places I was unsure about:
- Line 24 area: "A stretch target — the same rings carrying messages..." — chose colon ("A stretch target: the same rings...") since it explains what the target is, though a comma aside was also plausible.
- Line ~57-59: "so a panicking fill aborts rather than degrading; fine, but a property to design around." — chose comma + "which is fine, but ..." to keep it one sentence rather than splitting into a sentence fragment.
- Line ~288 ("CACHE_LINE_SIZE = 64 plays two roles — ... Apple M-series; Intel's adjacent-line prefetcher ...") — the inner semicolon between "Apple M-series" and "Intel's..." was inside a parenthetical list of examples, so I converted it to a comma rather than a period, treating it as a short parenthetical list item.

All lines within 100 columns. All target punctuation removed.

Summary: I edited /home/wink/data/prgs/rust/zc-ring-x1/tmp/rbd/c2.md, changing 26 lines (across roughly 20 edit operations) to remove semicolons, em dashes, en dashes, ellipses, and prose arrows per the rules, while leaving arrows/punctuation inside inline code spans untouched. Verification command now returns no matches, and no line exceeds 100 columns.

Uncertain spots (my judgment calls):
- Line ~230 ("only unwinding reaches it, since panic=abort targets never do.") — converted an em-dash aside into a comma+"since" causal clause rather than two sentences.
- Line ~146 area ("...phasing), and this section is the full design.") — joined via comma+"and" rather than splitting into two sentences.
- The "Batch release (resolves the batching question): deferred: the guard API..." now has two colons close together (one original, one from my em-dash conversion); kept as-is since it reads correctly, but flagging it as a borderline case.

Clean. No lines over 100 columns and no remaining offending punctuation in prose.

15 lines changed (across the edits above, spanning bullet leads, semicolon-joined lists, and one contrast semicolon). No places I was unsure about; all bold-label em-dash bullets converted to `- Label: text`, and semicolons were resolved per the rules (list-item end → period, contrast/list-joining semicolons → period or comma+conjunction as fit).

File: `/home/wink/data/prgs/rust/zc-ring-x1/tmp/rbd/c3.md`

The file already contains none of the target characters (no `;`, `—`, `–`, `…`, or `→`) anywhere, including in bullet leads like `- **Segments**:` which already use the colon form. Verified with the specified check command (no output) and a direct grep for each character (no output).

Lines changed: 0

Unsure about: nothing — verification command confirmed no target punctuation exists in the file.

Verification is clean.

1 line changed (line 258, rewrapped to two lines: 258-259). No uncertain cases.

96 lines changed.

Verification passed (grep found no remaining banned punctuation in prose outside code blocks/spans). File edited: /home/wink/data/prgs/rust/zc-ring-x1/tmp/rbd/c6.md

96 lines changed. No places I was unsure about — all substitutions followed the stated rules directly (bold+dash bullet labels converted to "Label: text", asides converted to commas/periods/parentheses, list-joining semicolons converted to periods/sub-bullets, arrows converted to "->").

All target punctuation removed; verification command returns no hits.

Lines changed: 2 (the two `## Resolved questions` bullets, spanning lines 110–121).

Unsure spots:
- Line 110: kept the resulting double colon ("Cross-process trust: resolved in 0.3.0-4: the ...") since the label itself is followed by a colon-introduced clause that was already there before the em dash; converting the em dash to ": " per rule 2 while leaving the pre-existing colon intact seemed the closest fit, but it does read as two colons in one sentence.
- Line 116: same double-colon situation for "`split()` once-guard: direction chosen: an ...".
